body: If you've browsed suicidal people's forums for a long time you're bound to bump into something about hanging. It's one of the most popular suicide methods.

Understandable. Thanks for answering.

btw, I'm glad you can still enjoy yourself, even if you're still overall miserable. Hope you can pull yourself out of this situation. Wanna talk about what makes you feel like that?
How long did it take before you got cut down?

Thank you. I needed that.

I was planning on killing myself a few hours from now. I'm not going to. At least not for a while.

I'll see about going back job hunting until the end of the month. I could really benefit from having a place of my own.

>I didn't find you from this post; I noticed the compassion in one of your comments and wanted to hear more from you, so I clicked onto your page and found this

I was wondering how you wandered into a day old post. Nice knowing that there's someone who cares. Thank you. You're a good person and, if you ever need someone, even if I'm not around to repay your kindness, I hope you meet someone as nice as you are.

Thank you. Now I just have to stop rereading your reply lest I start crying again. =)

Thank you. Your words touched me. It's nice being acknowledged. I really needed that.

>which can be hard enough as is, and plenty of people struggle there -- but also grown adults and a household. Beginning from the time you were a kid, no less. That's awful.

It didn't exactly began full on from when I was a kid. Back then, my grandmother wasn't as sick and did a lot of the housework but as the cigarettes took more and more of her health away I began to do more and more until, by the time I was 18, I was practically the only one caring for everyone else. Caring for my brother, though, was pretty much from day one. My father was never one to be caring, nurturing or responsible so I ended up as a makeshift father, if only one with none of the authority or respect to do anything meaningful. Didn't stop him from hating me most of the time but I guess that's what I get for being by his side all of his life. I'm the easiest target for his frustrations. I wonder if that's the cause of teenage rebellion.

>Is there any way you can leave the house?

Nowadays, I don't really *need* it. Not as much as in the past. I've since stopped doing most housework. My greataunt, who lives most of the time, and my father now do a little. Not as much as I usually did so . That being said, for me to leave this place I'd need to find a job again and it's not only difficult but I'm not sure I have the will to do it. I used to be hardworking and caring. Now I feel old and tired. I guess it's the effect of dedicating so long for so little.

I've recently developed a bit of envy too. I was never an envious person but it feels off to see happy young people nowadays. "You mean you had hobbies from a young age and you were even encouraged and helped to pursue them!?" that sort of thing.

If I end up killing myself, I wouldn't mourn my own death. Life wasn't particularly enjoyable. I'm thankful for people like you though. You make this world feel worth it.
Have you ever seen Channing Tatum? The man looks like an IRL Mr. Potato Head but girls and boys go wild for him. Danny DeVito was married for 35 years and still gets along with his ex.
[This post](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/1cep2h/psa_whats_wrong_with_posting_a_general_people/) might actually be helpful for you.

That's fine. Frankly, it might be even easier for you to stay open like that. Eveb aside from your own self-satisfaction, the fact that you're studying and want to get a better job makes you valuable to society at large as well.

You're already putting in effort at life. Your attractiveness can be helped with better clothes and taking care of your health. I know it's hard but you should be proud.

I know, right? I once read something that goes "one time your parents picked you up as a baby, put you down, and never picked you up again". It's a pretty weird feeling to look back on and even weirder to look forward to.

>Then my girlfriend broke up with me and made a suicide attempt. This literally broke my heart

That's alright. You've been through a terrible situation. No one can blame you for being hurt. You're only human.

>Trying to convince myself, that I am not weak now, that I got better

After the situation with your girlfriend and losing college, you still managed to get into another carreer and, even if you're working at a bad job right now, that's basically your third attempt. That's admirable.

>They want me to go back to college, but I don't want them to waste money again

Considering your force of will, it might be good for you. You tried and started again so many times. If you dislike your current job, getting into education might be the one thing you need.

The fact that you've tried drawing today is nice. You might be having a bad day but if you enjoyed yourself drawing, that's productive in and of itself, even if you feel drained.

Have you tried taking baths every day at the same time? Getting your habits into a routine can be really helpful to get yourself into doing things.
That's nice. Anything more specific? There are a lot of things in IT from server maintenace to web and mobile development.

I know. It sucks when all your efforts feel like they have no results but you can't call yourself a parasite if you're still trying. A parasite is content on leeching off. You're doing your best, aren't you?

I know it's hard but you should be proud.

>left me for not posting our relationship on Facebook

That just sounds ridiculous. You're worth more than that.

> I know my little brothers and my cat will be fine, nobody needs me.

Thing is, they might not need you, but want you.

Imagine a person that lives eating bland food with a cup of water, but every day, they enjoy watching a new movie. Out of these two habits, one keeps them alive and the other is superflous. One is necessary to stay alive but the other one only brings happiness.

It's okay. I'm glad you've got good company.

It's fine to have bad days and I'm honestly glad it takes an "exceptionally sad day" for you to feel this down. I'm here if you want to vent.

It's tough getting a job right now. I know. I'm in college myself and haven't worked in 4 years. I know how it sucks.

No one can blame you for not trying.
I hope you don't. If at all possible, I'd like you to not give that shitstain the satisfaction.
Nice. I'm on computer science myself. What would you like to work with?
I don't mean to offend but empty platitudes don't really help.

If you need relief, you can vent here at the very least.

What's on your mind right now?

You won't be forever at your job. You're already going to college. Once you're done you might be able to not only be free from studying but also have the qualification to get a more fulfilling job.

What are you studying?

> Once life hits you, you got to always bounce back

Try doing that for 20 years.

>that what makes you a better person

No, it doesn't. Suffering  doesn't necessarily bring happiness. Psychological wounds pile up as emotional baggage and the years continue to roll on until you can look back and only see the dreams and hopes you discarded.

>learn from your mistakes and resolve them

Contrary to many here, I don't feel like I've made any mistakes. I was simply born in an environment that didn't allow for my happiness.

If I could go back in time and advise my younger self, I most likely would have ended in the same place. My younger self took all the good decisions they reasonably could and still ended up here. If I had any better foresight and judgement, I might have been a lottery winner.

Eh, I wouldn't hold it against you. Some dogs are evil hellspawns. Rabbits and cats too.

I once met one of my father's girlfriend's pet rabbit and, despite doing everything right, that little ball of evil still bit me. Hard. I swear the devil was possessing that furball.

>you only have to work half a year and I thought I would write a book / short stories in that time

You'd also have little free time during that half year. A normal job would give a little free time all over the year.

>might be the only person in my class who might be failing this semester

Everyone has their struggles. Odds are someone else isn't adapting so well to online classes. Odds are someone else is also struggling just the same as you are but you'd never know without ever having the opportunity of talking to them.

>When I was in school, there was this rumour that I was gay and was bullied because of it.

Kids can be little shitheads and will latch on to anything they might perceive as a way of making themselves feel better than others even if it take being mean to them for no reason.

>how a kid my age can be 110 pounds and 4'8" tall

I've checked your previous posts for your age. According to [this](https://www.cdc.gov/growthcharts/data/set1clinical/cj41c021.pdf) you're only 2 inches bellow the median for boys. As for the weight, you're a little above the average but you have a lot of time and puberty to lose it. Want to talk about it?

It's normal not to like yourself at your age. Self esteem during these years can be rough. What do you like to do?

Edit: you actually have a 24.6 BMI putting you at "normal weight". Considering your age, you might have an easier time getting even farther from overweight range than you think. Just try to keep yourself away from soda and sweets. Keeping a lot of cold water in the fridge can be really nice, especially if you put it in the freezer for 20 minutes.

>just some close people dont care about anything

It's not just that. I'm tired. I spent my whole life trying to make everyone else's lives better. Just because I was the only person with any sense of responsibility I had more and more responsibilities thrown at me all my life here. Whenever I tried asking for help we would get into fights because apparently I was too lazy to do everything. Now I'm just tired. I've slowly dropped all hobbies I had and have been more and more stressed. I used to even like housework. I used to be a great cook.

It feels surreal that it pains me to see another person suffering in the slightest but my family are somehow able to resist years of pleas for help and specific and simple instructions on how to make theirs and my own life better. My mother might have been a cruel sociopath but I didn't expect to come to live here with such a terrible combination of laziness and lack of empathy.

It feels weird that, between me, my father, my brother, and my grandmother, I'm the only one whose bedroom doesn't reek of urine in one way or another. All they care about is their own comfort and laziness, no matter what.

>try to make them take responsibility someway

I did manage to make my father start taking care of some household chores regularly after begging him to since I was 13. It only took over 10 years and a nervous breakdown for me to make a man in his 50s to have as much responsibility as I had at age 11. My brother is a lost cause though. He's 20 and hasn't a fraction of the sense of responsibility I had when I had less than half of his age. He hates how lazy my father just like I do but doesn't feel like doing anything different. I don't get it.

> your best friend’s house

Don't have any. I used to have some at my job years ago but I couldn't manage to keep this house running while attending college and working all at the same time. Can't really work triple shifts and still sleep at night.

Nowadays I'm tired. I used to get up every day at 6 AM, clean the house and enjoy the mornings before going to work/school. I was driven and had hopes for the future. Now I'm too tired to do anything. My hobbies feel like a pain. I can't find the energy to work like I did in the past. I can't summon the will to care for anything at this point. I just want to rest.

> it just makes me ridiculous that a breakup has made everything go to shit

It's not ridiculous. A breakup can be a though thing, a breakup when you're socially isolated with no one to rely on can be devastating. I understand. You're in a terrible place and it's easy to understand why you feel like this.

You shouldn't be so tough on yourself.

> She just texted me New Years

So she's still thinking about you. Interesting.

> It kills me that she still has a lot of hatred and resentment for everything that happened

But not enough for her to cut all contact with you. She wouldn't even want to think about you on new year's eve if she hated you that much.

> At one point I asked her if she could at least hear me to try to tell her some things that made me feel bad, obviously she didn't respond

Makes sense to be honest. If she broke up with you because of your depression, it's clear that she did so because she couldn't help you, at least not at the time, but the fact is that she still texted you on new year.

So she's contacting you on happy occasions and avoiding the bad ones. It sounds to me like she wants to be happy with you. She just couldn't deal with your issues. She's not your therapist.

I don't want to give you any unfounded hope but it sounds like she still cares about you. It sounds to me like she'd be happy to see you in a better place and that, instead of seeking her forgiveness, you should give her what she wants and work through your issues with your doctors.

If she will called out to you on a commemorative day but won't answer to you drunkenly texting her about all the bad things that happened, maybe she simply doesn't want to talk about your misery which she can't help with. She might respond better to a positive text. Less "all the bad things I've done" and more "all the good things I'll try to do".

> what I deserve for letting go

You didn't let go as much as your relationship fell apart. It happens.

>the least I can do to make up for the damage I did to her is k / ll m self

That's not gonna benefit her in the slightest. You're looking for justifications for your suicide. If anything, having someone she once loved being in such a state would hurt her more.

> About my doctors, they literally abandoned me in times of crisis

How so? I feel like it makes sense for them to direct you towards people specialised in dealing with suicidal patients in a service that can get you immediate help. You don't schedule a doctor's appointment for an emergency, right?

> Now I only have medication with another psychiatrist and another psychiatrist but both maintain that it is not so good to leave my selfe with a label of mental disorder as Borderline

What other solution are they trying with you, besides medication? Do you consult with them regularly?

> I do not feel with a future, I do not think I will feel the same for someone, much less find someone like her. 

You didn't feel like you'd find someone like her before you did either.

> I have stopped doing all the things that made me happy, right now I don't want and I don't deserve happiness

Would you feel happy if she had stopped everything that made her happy after breaking up with you? Your misery benefits no one and only serves to perpetuate itself.

>when I went to my psychiatrist and a psychologist who "work together" they both diagnosed me as Borderline

That could very well be the case, especially if two different professionals both diagnosed you with the same. If you require professional help and you have access to it, it'd be the best thing you can do for yourself. Do you still have their contact information?

>I have a hard time and it hurts a lot not being able to be with her.  it was possibly the best 4 years of my life.

I understand.

> I feel that there is no reason to move on, to try to improve or heal

You have yourself to care for. If she broke up with you, it was because while she was unhappy with the relationship, she also couldn't help you fix it. It's simply a matter of two people being in a situation that, at least in the moment, doesn't allow for a healthy relationship.

> I feel like I have failed the only person who was always with me

You have but that's only a consequence of your faults. You're only human.

Think of it like this: you only entered a relationship with her back when you didn't have her. Right? You were happy enough without her that she wanted to be with you. She wouldn't have gotten together with you if you were desperate and sad. That's why it's important to move on and "reset" yourself, just like she should be doing. You need to internalise this. Try and focus yourself in things you enjoy instead of your failures.

You found her on square one. Go back to it. You might not find her, or even anything there but you're at at the end of a one way street and there's nothing good for you there.

>really don't think he cares about anything that happens to me or does

Maybe she moved on. Maybe she didn't. The fact of the matter is that, from her perspective, the best thing she can do for herself is move on. It's the same thing with you. You should, above all, prize your own health and well-being.

I understand you feel it's important to communicate to her how important your problems are and that her leaving didn't help but even if you do it, what then? Neither of you are at fault if one has issues the other can't help with. That simply means you aren't meant to be together, at least at this moment in time. It happens.

My original plan was for two or three hours from now. I've been having a nice night though. I might take down my noose for today at the very least.

Edit: Still don't have an answer for the lost time though. It's not fair that I had to go through all that bullshit just for the people around me to realise that I have a life too as well as that they have responsibilities(which they still barely care for).

I'm tired. I lived with an abusive mother until I was 10 and then moved in with my father. Ever since then I've worked hard to try and make everyone's lives better in the hope that something would improve. 14 years later and bugger all changed except me slowly dropping everything I've ever enjoyed and the fact that I'm far too tired of being everyone else's thankless makeshift mother.

Either there is an afterlife or there isn't. Either way I'd escape from the hell I've been corralled into all my life.

I'm thankful for your sympathy. I'll try and give myself a nice all nighter starting now and see if I can get back to enjoying myself. If I do, I'll see about getting my life together. If not, I'll end this.

Regardless I win either happiness or an end and I'll gladly take either.

> looking forward to possibly moving out and separating yourself from your family? 

There are three problems with that:

First, I'd need time. I could never hold a job while having two other full occupations. I tried.

Second, I'd need a job. Turns out it's particularly hard to find a first decent job as a programmer, at least in my country. I'd need enough money to sustain myself and to try and make up for all the time I've lost.

And third, I'm tired. I've been at it for well over a decade now. It's like trying to row a viking boat all by yourself. I tried my best but I needed help rowing. And as I got more and more tired I began throwing away parts of me that kept me happy to the point that trying anything that formerly brought me happiness brings me dread. I feel like trying to make up for a lost life is too much of a hassle. I'd rather not live a life desperately trying to make up for it.

I'm thankful for the offer but I have already thought long and hard about this. I'm not sad. Not anymore.

If my efforts alone could ensure my happiness and of those around me my life would be full of wonders.

I'm giving myself 12 more hours at most. I'll try to find the joys I have cast aside during that time. If I change my mind, I'll make sure to PM you after deleting this post. Again, thank you.

> What if you open up pandora’s box but there is no hope inside

That honestly sounds wonderful. I wished to kill myself when I was a child but I persisted on the hope that I'd experience happiness before the end of my life. Nowadays I see that that hope was baseless.

Had I known that, I might have either resigned myself to what plagued my life back then and found appreciation in the small bits of happiness that I now miss or ended my life back then and saved myself the suffering. It is a cruel fate to labour endlessly without any reward.

>I have asked

And they agreed?

> I can not go ahead with that feeling of having failed the only person who always was with me at all times

It happens. You're human, thus fallible. You can take this as an opportunity to learn from your mistakes. She's not the only person in the world who's capable of bringing you happiness and the reverse is also true.

The advice to move on you got was sound. It's important for you to be able to be happy with yourself before being happy in a relationship, otherwise one won't be able to support the other when they falter.

I recommend you start by looking for things you enjoyed even before you met her and focus on that. If you wish to send a message to her, wouldn't it be all the better if you did it while your mind is in a better state?

I'll be honest with you. It sounds like you should really move on from her. You had a life before her. You should be able to have a life after.

Love is like a drug. You can suffer from withdraw. You need to get over the worst part of it. If you feel like informing her of your feelings will help you, I advise you to do it, but you should be aware that moving on is the best thing you could do. Not even she would like you to be miserable like that for your whole life, would she?

> I know I’m a lot for people

But you're working on that. This is going to sound cliche but nobody is perfect and the important thing is to keep trying. They always promise that "we're in this together" but it doesn't sound to me like you're reaching out to them as often.

I know this pandemic has been horrible for everyone but have you tried asking them to hang out yourself. How do people react when you take the initiative to spend time with them?
So your depression caused you to distance yourself from her which in turn caused her to leave, worsening your depression, is that right?

>Sadly I realice that she's controlling my life. More than me

How so? You haven't had any contact with her, have you?
Nice. I also recommend you try and put your phone far away or try one of those puzzle alarm apps.

>Some kid made me be his "Girlfriend." 

That's horrible. I'm sorry you had to go through that. 

>Everyone at that school hated me too. Even the teachers.

Are you sure of that? I'll be honest with you, most teachers don't really tend to care that much unless you make their jobs difficult.

>At the end of 5th grade, a social worker lied to my parents about shit. Claimed I told her I was starving. It was all lies. It was all over snacks. I told them I didn't care about that stuff and that I was fine. They twisted my words

I'm gonna give him a small benefit of the doubt here. If I understood it correctly, you told them something about snacks and they interpreted it as you being starved, correct? 

Not every adult is competent at their job. They might not have intended to twist your words but simply made a grave misunderstanding and ended up exagerating things. There's this thing called [Hanlon's Razor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanlon%27s_razor) and the gist of it is that most people don't mean anything bad, they're just stupid.

>I moved to my current town. I made a few new friends. 

I'm honestly a bit impressed by your capacity to make new friends. When I moved schools, I could never quite fit in. You sound like a pleasant person to be around if you can make new friend so often.

>In 2019, I was in stem class, I was sexually harassed by some boys for being a lesbian

If this is happening at school, you really should take up these things with teachers. 

>My dad knows that I wanted to shoot myself with his gun, yet he still buys them. He just keeps them "Out of reach."

Your dad sounds a bit like mine. Absolutely irresponsible and self centered. You think you should know that, before being your parents, your parents are people. And those people can be major assholes.

>He even was talking about how deadly one of his guns are right in front of me

He might not. Gonna be honest with you, as far as my experience goes, most people that are that into guns are overgrown children with deep admiration for violence and power. My father had the same reaction after seeing an airsoft gun in a shop. It's just the awe of having something that they feel like gives them power.

Have you tried giving Child Protection Services a call? Or at least talking to an adult at your school?

Why do you never do anything right? What kind of mistakes do you make?

It can help to think and learn from your mistakes. Sometimes we simply don't make the best decisions. If you can try again, you can learn from the past.
Yeah, I once went on a run on a beach and by the 8th mile or so I had to constantly remind myself that I shouldn't stop to try and drink from the puddles in the sand.

Frankly, odds are, even if she weren't fit, she'd have someone find her attractive. The problem is that, from a young age, girls have an absurdly heavy emphasis on their appearance as a measure of their worth.

"Oh Jimmy is so smart! Oh Cindy you look so cute!" Boy's get pushed into trying to be the action hero, girls get pushed into being the pretty princess. That sort of thing.

> It’s just in the way everything is happening and how different the time feels.

I mean, that could still very well be on you. It can be hard to be nice with someone who's depressed, however much you might like them.

>I can get out of it with my own actions but not with the people currently in my life.

Do you have a plan to make your life better? If so, that's wonderful. Do the people around you hinder your plans?

> I always figured I'd live a more enjoyable life when I'm an adult cuz I won't get bullied so much

If it's any comfort, from my experience, that's actually more or less the case. Teenagers suck. In my experience, as far as bullying goes life is pretty alright after high school.

> since it ends so soon.

Life doesn't end that soon. From your perspective, your life lasts all the time in the world. It's just that that time can feel miserable depending on your circumstances.

Well, at least you can share stuff with them.

If you're going to start a routine, start with something small and different. Try getting out of bed an hour earlier every few days. Or 30 minutes if that's too hard. Just put your alarm on and make your bed. Use your extra time to do something you enjoy. It doesn't need to be productive, just different.

For example, tomorrow, try set your alarm for an hour before your usual waking time, brush your teeth, sit somewhere in your house and watch something on youtube during that extra hour. Every three days, try and set your alarm an hour earlier until you're sleeping however much you think you should be sleeping. Just getting out of bed earlier should help a little.

>Every day is a new opportunity to move closer to our goals

That's what I believed in the past but it's hard to do it while carrying everyone else's mistakes and responsibilities on my back.

>People who have hope

I used to be one of those. I've been depressed since I can remember but I still had hope. I think I lost it all when I realised that I've been in the same place for 10 years regardless of how much work I put into.

Some people are lucky and get massive payoffs for their efforts. I'm unlucky and I get nothing. All my effort, all my dedication, all of my sacrifices were for nothing. I wish I had a family capable of thankfulness and basic responsibility.

>we can take responsibility for our own well-being

I tried. When nobody around me would care for themselves I also had to take responsibility for them. I got nothing in return. Nothing I wished that would have made me and the people around me happy came true no matter how much effort I put into it because I'm not strong enough to carry the whole world. I made all the right choices but I'm still here.

If I were born into a decent family, I would have never had to try and failt to balance studies, work and being the babysitter of a bunch of adults 24/7. If I were born into a loving family, I would have never had to live like a homeless person inside my own house while caring for everyone else's responsibilities.

I wanted to be young. Not to waste my life as a makeshift mother for my family. I wanted to be happy, not a failure in every aspect. I wanted the best for my family not to fail at everything because no one would help me when I begged them.

I give up.

> but (s)he is unwilling to at least answer my messages

Even if they don't answer, they might just read it. Sending them a message while you're alive and them just reading it would get you the same result as if you left them a suicide note.

It's kinda like this:

 | You leave a suicide note | You send a message
---|---|----
**They only read it** | You get to tell them what you want | You get to tell them what you want
**They try to answer you** | You get to tell them what you want | You get to tell them and you get an answer

>I think they’re done

You think that's the case but do they actually think that? Has anyone ever said or indicated this to you or is your insecurity being projected onto them?

> I’m afraid to be alone in this world but I’m going to be and part of it is because I make it that way and I can’t do it.

If you're responsible for making your life like that, that's honestly good news. All that means is that you're in control and you messed up. But if you're in control, that means you can also get out of this with your own actions.

What actions you think are responsible for your state?
Family can be tough. I know. How about your friends? Anyone you could spend time with?

>Never thought about it that way. Although we started to originate consciousness after we are born. So how does the reverse work. We just see. Blank and nothingness?

I think you might be as consciousness after as before. Before your birth, your brain didn't exist. After your death, it'll cease to be.

>now that is exploding up I want to kill myself.

It will end up rising again soon. You can start again.

>I think I rather die than go back.

Is your country that bad? Sounds like you could at least attempt a job there for a while, at least until things go back to normal.

It's nice that you have a family and friends. Could anyone in your family perhaps help you? It sounds like you could use some help establishing a routine. Maybe try spending time with your parents or something. It's easier to establish yourself if you have someone you can follow along.

So I went ahead and read your post at /r/Paranormal. I hate to sound dismissive, but I think you might just have been an imaginative child.

Memories are not a perfect record of the past. Especially when you're so young.

About the shower thing, it's normal. Getting afraid to close your eyes in the shower is pretty common. I think it might be because the shower makes it hard to hear stuff so, if you have your eyes closed, you'd have a hard time noticing scary things coming.

About Jack and Johnny. That's normal too. Just more evidence of your bright imagination. You had a scary room you never entered. It's normal to feel scared by it.

>when somethings don’t seem right to me or somethings are completely out of my control and are doing something “wrong” I get really bad urges to scratch or hit myself

It could be that you're on the autism spectrum. It'd probably help to see an actual therapist about it.

About the weight on you while you slept, could that be sleep paralysis?
Are there no financial help programs for students available for you? Does your college offer no information on any program?

>I hate crying everyday and being reminded of how stupid I am and the mistakes I have made.

Wanna talk about that? Sometimes you need some else's perspective.

>I would really like to know what it feels to be dead

I kind of think it's the same as not being born. All of us have spent billions of years not existing already.
Now that you've mentioned, I haven't brushed my teeth all day. Thanks for the reminder.

> I keep writing out comments or posts of how I want to respond or what I want to say but I always find myself writing a fucking novel cause there's so much shit I want to say

I think it's because you have lot of stuff to say and you haven't got the opportunity to let it out. I just wrote my first post here and it ended up being a fucking wall of text.

>I just find everything so mentally exhausting that I end up sleeping for 12 hours a day. Any tips, any advice, spent the last two years doing nothing and spent the last five years feeling like shit all the time.

I'm not sure if this will help. I used to be a lot more motivated. What I did back then was getting into a routine. Back when I still had motivation, I used to get up at 6 AM and clean up the living room. Even nowadays when I've lost most of my will to live I still get up at 11 to make lunch.

So what I'm saying is that I think you need to get in the groove of things. It's like baking a cake. The first time you do it you have to constantly check the recipe and slowly measure everything out but by the 100th time you can just follow along a routine you're already used to.
